newsitem.title: UK: Milky Way has halo of dark matter, experts say.
newsitem.headline: Milky Way has halo of dark matter, experts say.

text.p: The Earth's own Milky Way galaxy is surrounded by an invisible halo of mysterious "dark matter", British astronomers reported on Tuesday.
Robert Olling and Michael Merrifield of Southampton University said measurements of hydrogen gas in the galaxy showed the invisible dark matter must be distributed like a hollow sphere.
They told the annual National Astronomy Meeting in Southampton that their findings could change some basic assumptions about galaxy formation.

Measurements of the universe indicate that there must be a lot more material in it than can be accounted for by visible stars, galaxies and other objects. Scientists believe that "dark matter" -- so-called because it cannot be seen -- could make up a large percentage of matter in the universe.
Although dark matter cannot be seen, its effects can. Like all mass it has a gravitational pull and the effects on nearby objects or material can be measured.
Olling and Merrifield measured the amount of visible hydrogen gas and how it is laid out, and found it is in a thick layer.
This must mean the dark matter is spread out in a diffuse halo -- otherwise it would flatten out the gas into a thin layer, they said.
Most astronomers predicted that dark matter must be strongly flattened -- so the findings could change theories about how galaxies formed, Olling and Merrifield said.
